Report of the General Manager
Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency Update
items.text: Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency Update Nicole Sandkulla, Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency (BAWSCA) CEO discussed (1) Negotiation of a new Tier Two Drought Allocation Plan that is being considered by BAWSCA members that will determine how the 2026 Wholesale Customers share the available supplies from the SFPUC’s system during a drought. She discussed the current Tier Two Pan which was adopted in 2009 and expired in 2018, with yearly extensions by the BAWSCA Board. She discussed details of the new Tier Two Plan and indicated that negotiations are expected to conclude by the end of this fiscal year; (2) Development of the scope for the Long-term Reliable Water Supply Strategy 2045 which will take approximately six months. She noted monthly engagement with member agencies, Board Policy Committee, and BAWSCA Board of Directors; and (3) Fall 2023 Water Efficient Landscape Education Series that will offer more than 20 free classes to the public, both virtually and in person. She indicated there is also a library of virtual classes for public viewing. President Ajami thanked CEO Sandkulla for the presentation and for information on the educational classes. CEO Sandkulla discussed the success of the courses and public participation levels

items.title: Award Contract Nos. PRO.0240.A-B, Racial Equity Consulting to AECOM Technical Services, Inc. (PRO.0240.A) for an amount not-to-exceed $9,500,000 with a term of five years
items.text: Award Contract Nos. PRO.0240.A-B, Racial Equity Consulting to AECOM Technical Services, Inc. (PRO.0240.A) and Rosales Business Partners and GCAP Services, Joint Venture (PRO.0240.B), each for an amount not-to-exceed $9,500,000 with a term of five years, for as- needed racial equity consulting and support services to assist with implementation of the agency’s Racial Equity Action Plan, Racial Justice Resolution and other racial equity priorities. dr. bijoux noted the importance of the work to be performed under the proposed contracts. He discussed the Seven Pillars contained in the Racial Equity Action Plan, indicating the work to be performed is intricate and that internal capacity needs to be developed to perform the work in the large SFPUC organization. He stated consultants are needed to help staff conduct the necessary work to build the infrastructure required to carry out the important work. GM Herrera stated this is the first major contract in this area. He recognized the importance of the work that will be performed under the direct supervision him and dr. bijoux and state the consultant’s work will be task-order based and will be closely monitored. In response to a question from VP Maxwell for an example of the work to be performed by AECOM, dr. bijoux responded that work would include AECOM’s assistance with mapping every activity in the SFPUC, with efforts to achieve more collaboration and less isolation, and to break down existing silos

items.title: Public hearing to consider and possible action to adopt amendments to the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission’s Social Impact Partnership Program Rules and Regulations, at Rule 1.0 and Rule 4.5. (Ordikhani)
items.text: Public hearing to consider and possible action to adopt amendments to the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission’s Social Impact Partnership Program Rules and Regulations, at Rule 1.0 and Rule 4.5. Valerie Tulier-Laiwa, Manager, Social Impact Partnership Program (SIP) provided a brief summary of the SIP. She noted a recent citywide suspension order prohibiting several entities from applying to and receiving future city contracts, and that the Mayor directed departments to cancel contracts with those entities. She stated the proposed amendment to the Rules and Regulations comply with the Mayor’s directive and were drafted in partnership with the City Attorney. She discussed proposed Rule 1.0 and Rule 4.5 amendments, stating they are technical in nature to comply with the city-wide directive
